history.period: Built 1909 (National Mission on Monuments and Antiquities record PB16017586 lists 'C. 20th Cent. CE', sub-period 1909)
history.summary: IDENTITY NOTE: the CSV name 'Shiv Mandir' is generic; the best-supported referent in Barnala town is the Pracheen (Prachin) Shiv Mandir near the railway station, locally known as the Chaudhary Temple. Local tradition (reported by myadhyatm.com) says the Shivalinga was carried on his head from Kashi to Barnala barefoot by a devotee named Fakir Chand, and that Maharaja Bhupinder Singh of Patiala conferred the title 'Chaudhary' on his brother Ramji Das, the temple's caretaker - hence the name Chaudhary Temple. The NMMA record confirms the temple was built by the Chaudhari Ram Ji Das Charitable Trust in the colonial era (1909). Devotees believe wishes of true devotees are fulfilled here; the first rays of the sun are said to fall on the Shivalinga. Fairs and bhandaras are held on Maha Shivaratri and in Shravan, with kanwariyas bringing Ganga water from Haridwar. Correction: the NMMA record lists the district as Sangrur, but that predates 2006 - Barnala has been a separate district since 2006, so district is corrected to Barnala. Coordinates are from a place-listing entry (approximate - verify before visiting).

name: Shiv Mandir
town_description: Barnala is the headquarters of Barnala district, Punjab (a separate district since 2006, carved out of Sangrur). It sits at about 227 m elevation on the plains of Malwa, connected by rail and road to Bathinda, Ludhiana, Sangrur and Mansa.

travel.airport: Chandigarh International Airport, about 150 km away (verify).
travel.railway: Barnala Junction railway station; the temple is described as being near the railway station.
travel.road: Reached by road within Barnala town; the town lies on major road links between Bathinda, Ludhiana, Sangrur and Mansa.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Maha Shivaratri and the Shravan/Sawan period for festivals (large crowds).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM daily by a place listing - verify before visiting. Mondays see long queues.
